title: The Bricks Standard: vendor guide
intro: Calm, composed and true. Follow these steps on every job. Diagrams use metres and seconds.

diagrams.title: Camera height: lens at 1.2 to 1.4 metres, camera level
Keeping verticals straight: tilted versus level camera
Slow push-in path, 0.6 to 1.2 metres at 15 cm/s maximum
Pan arc of 15 to 40 degrees at 5 degrees per second maximum
Drone rise from 3 m to 30 to 45 m at 1 m/s maximum
Drone orbit, 45 to 90 degrees at 5 degrees per second maximum
Camera positions in a room: two corners and the doorway
Window light and time of day
Clip duration bar: hold 2 s, move, hold 2 s
Virtual Visit walking path: loop each room, cross doorways twice
Virtual Visit walking speed, about 0.5 m/s
Virtual Visit phone height, 1.3 to 1.4 m, ultra-wide

steps.title: Show up for every job you accept
steps.body:
You can hand back a job up to 48 hours before. After that, or if you don't check in within 30 minutes of the window start, your Bricks account ends. Emergencies are excepted, and completed work is always paid.

Once a job is yours, you do it yourself. Hand it back in the app at least 48 hours before the start and Bricks will reassign it. Check in on site within 100 m of the property. Checking in more than 30 minutes after the start counts as a no-show, even if you finish the job. You won't get new jobs and can't apply again, but jobs you've completed are still paid.

When you cancel, pick the reason. A medical emergency, bereavement, an accident or breakdown on the way, severe weather or unsafe drone conditions, an unsafe site or no access at the property, or a Bricks app or GPS outage goes to Bricks for review instead of closing your account. If your account is closed, you can appeal within 7 days by emailing help@brxs.ca. This is amendment A1 of your contractor agreement (IC-A1 v1.0).
do: Accept only the jobs you can do
Hand a job back at least 48 hours before the start
Check in in the app within 100 m of the property
dont: Cancel inside 48 hours unless it's an emergency
Send someone else in your place
Skip the check-in

steps.title: Open the job
steps.body: Check the package, property type and footprint in the app. Your shot list and clip list load from these.
do: Read every item on both lists
Note anything marked as a client request
dont: Arrive without checking which package was booked

steps.title: Plan around the light
steps.body: Check which way the front of the home faces. Book your exterior time for when the sun is on the facade.
steps.diagram_alt: Window light and time of day
do: East-facing: shoot the front in the morning
West-facing: shoot the front in the afternoon
North-facing: bright overcast or twilight
dont: Shoot the hero exterior into the sun

steps.title: Pack the right kit
steps.body: Stills and clips need a dedicated camera. Virtual Visit needs an approved phone.
do: Camera, 16–24 mm and 35–50 mm lenses, tripod
Gimbal or slider for clips, ND filters, grey card
Spare batteries and cards, charged approved phone
dont: Bring a phone as your stills or clip camera

steps.title: Check the airspace
steps.body: For drone jobs, check the airspace and record any authorization in the app before you leave.
do: Mark drone clips "not possible" early if authorization is not in place
Tell Bricks before the shoot
dont: Fly in controlled airspace without permission

steps.title: Confirm the prep
steps.body: The app sends the homeowner a prep guide. Message or call if access, parking or prep is unclear.
do: Confirm pets, cars and access
Confirm building permission for amenities and drone
dont: Assume the home will be ready

steps.title: Walk the home first
steps.body: Walk every room before you shoot. Plan your order around the light.
do: Start with rooms that have the best light now
Note issues before you start
dont: Start shooting in the first room you see

steps.title: Prepare each room
steps.body: Tidy each room before you shoot it. Clear, calm and lived-in, not empty.
do: Clear counters to one or two objects
Toilet seats down, beds made, cords hidden
Bins, shoes and pet bowls out of shot
dont: Move heavy furniture
Handle valuables

steps.title: Set lights and blinds
steps.body: Turn on lights that match in colour. Open blinds to the same height.
do: Lights on and matched
Fans off, TVs off or black
dont: Mix warm and cool bulbs in one frame

steps.title: Set camera height
steps.body: Put the lens between 1.2 and 1.4 m for most rooms. Kitchens about 1.2 m.
steps.diagram_alt: Camera height: lens at 1.2 to 1.4 metres, camera level
do: Measure once and mark your tripod
Counter and table details at 1.0–1.1 m
dont: Shoot from eye level above 1.5 m indoors
Shoot from the floor

steps.title: Level the camera
steps.body: Keep the camera level, with no tilt up or down. Walls must stand straight.
steps.diagram_alt: Keeping verticals straight: tilted versus level camera
do: Use the level in your camera
Keep verticals within 0.5°
dont: Tilt down to show more floor
Plan to fix verticals in the edit

steps.title: Choose your positions
steps.body: Shoot most rooms from a corner. Shoot symmetrical spaces from the doorway or the centre.
steps.diagram_alt: Camera positions in a room: two corners and the doorway
do: Two corners for living, kitchen and primary bedroom
Doorway or centre for bathrooms and halls
dont: Shoot from behind a door or in a tight corner

steps.title: One-point or two-point
steps.body: One-point: square to the back wall, centred. Two-point: from a corner, two walls in view.
do: Choose one on purpose for each frame
dont: Stand almost square to a wall, so it looks like a mistake

steps.title: Use the right lens
steps.body: Use 16–24 mm (full-frame equivalent) for rooms. Use 35–85 mm for details.
do: Small rooms: shoot from the doorway at 16 mm
dont: Go wider than 16 mm
Stretch rooms to look bigger

steps.title: Bracket every frame
steps.body: Tripod always. Shoot 5 frames at 2 EV apart, plus one frame for the window view.
do: f/7.1–f/11, base ISO
Add a bounced flash frame where light is mixed
dont: Shoot handheld
Move the tripod between brackets

steps.title: Check windows and reflections
steps.body: Views should show detail. Check every mirror and glass surface for you or your gear.
do: Look at the window frame at 100% after a test shot
dont: Leave yourself in a mirror
Blow out a view that matters

steps.title: Shoot the details
steps.body: Shoot 3–6 detail images per job: hardware, materials, light on a surface.
do: Use 35–85 mm
Keep details simple and clean
dont: Shoot clutter close up

steps.title: Shoot the hero exterior
steps.body: The hero is the first image. Two-point, whole building, sun on the facade.
steps.diagram_alt: Window light and time of day
do: Sky about one third of the frame
Cars out, garage closed, bins away
dont: Shoot it against the sun
Leave people or cars in frame

steps.title: Capture for the edit
steps.body: You capture, Bricks edits. Give the editor everything: full brackets, a window pull and the room as it truly is.
do: Move bins, hoses and cords out of frame on site
Keep every frame of each set
dont: Edit, apply a preset or merge brackets
Hide damage, neighbours or permanent features
Stage a fake view, fire or TV image

steps.title: Shoot only the clip list
steps.body: Capture the clip IDs in the app. Bricks does all editing, grading, music and titles.
do: Follow the framing note for each clip ID
dont: Edit, grade or add music
Add extra moves that are not on the list

steps.title: Set capture settings
steps.body: 23.976p, shutter 1/48 or 1/50, UHD or higher, 10-bit log, ProRes 422 or 10-bit H.265.
do: Use ND filters to keep the shutter in daylight
59.94p at 1/120 only on clips marked "slow allowed"
dont: Shoot 25p or 50p
Use phones for clips

steps.title: Lock everything
steps.body: Set white balance, exposure and focus by hand, then lock them. Shoot a 3-second grey card clip in each lighting zone.
do: Manual Kelvin, same value for the same light
Name the grey card clip REF-WB
dont: Use auto white balance, auto exposure or autofocus
Zoom during a clip

steps.title: Locked-off clips
steps.body: Tripod. Frame it like a still. Record 10 seconds with nothing moving.
do: Keep verticals straight
Wait for light changes to finish
dont: Touch the camera while recording

steps.title: Push-in and slide
steps.body: Move in a straight line at an even speed, no faster than 15 cm per second. Travel 0.6–1.2 m.
steps.diagram_alt: Slow push-in path, 0.6 to 1.2 metres at 15 cm/s maximum
do: Use a slider or gimbal
Ease in and ease out
dont: Walk with the camera
Push past the subject

steps.title: Slow pan
steps.body: Pan no faster than 5° per second, 15–40° in total. A 30° pan takes at least 6 seconds.
steps.diagram_alt: Pan arc of 15 to 40 degrees at 5 degrees per second maximum
do: Use a fluid head or gimbal
Pan toward the light or the view
dont: Whip pan
Pan back and forth

steps.title: Hold before and after
steps.body: Hold still for 2 seconds, move, then hold still for 2 seconds. Moving clips run 10–12 seconds.
steps.diagram_alt: Clip duration bar: hold 2 s, move, hold 2 s
do: Count the holds out loud
dont: Cut the recording as the move ends

steps.title: Shoot the vertical clips
steps.body: Some clips are also needed in 9:16. Rotate the camera and shoot them natively.
do: Add _V to the clip ID
Keep the subject centred
dont: Crop a horizontal clip and call it vertical

steps.title: Record room tone
steps.body: Record 30 seconds of silence in the main living space. Name it REF-TONE.
do: Ask everyone to stay still and quiet
dont: Talk, walk or run appliances you can turn off

steps.title: Pre-flight
steps.body: Carry your certificate and registration. Survey the site and check wind and weather.
do: Stay in visual line of sight
Stay below 122 m above ground
dont: Fly over people unless your certificate and drone allow it

steps.title: Top-down
steps.body: Hover at 40–60 m with the camera pointing straight down. Keep the whole lot in frame.
do: Square the lot lines to the frame
Record 10 seconds
dont: Drift or rotate while recording

steps.title: Rise
steps.body: Face the home and rise straight up from 3 m to 30–45 m. No faster than 1 m per second.
steps.diagram_alt: Drone rise from 3 m to 30 to 45 m at 1 m/s maximum
do: Keep the camera level
Hold 2 seconds at the start and end
dont: Descend
Dive toward the home

steps.title: Orbit
steps.body: Circle the home at a constant 20–30 m height. No faster than 5° per second and 2 m per second.
steps.diagram_alt: Drone orbit, 45 to 90 degrees at 5 degrees per second maximum
do: Keep the home centred
Cover 45–90°
dont: Spin fast
Change height during the orbit

steps.title: Context push
steps.body: Fly slowly toward the home from the neighbourhood, no faster than 2 m per second. Stop short of it.
do: Start 30–60 m high
dont: Fly through gaps or under trees
Linger on neighbouring yards

steps.title: Abort if unsure
steps.body: If anything feels wrong, land. A safe abort never lowers your score.
do: Mark the clip "not possible" with a reason
dont: Push on in high wind or poor visibility

steps.title: Open guided capture
steps.body: Use an approved phone and open guided capture in the app. Follow the on-screen steps.
do: Let the app lock exposure, focus and white balance
Shoot after stills, while the home is styled
dont: Use the phone's own camera app
Zoom in

steps.title: Hold the phone right
steps.body: Follow the on-screen steps. Hold the phone upright at chest height, about 1.3–1.4 m, on the 0.5× lens.
steps.diagram_alt: Virtual Visit phone height, 1.3 to 1.4 m, ultra-wide
do: Keep it level
Turn your body, not your wrist
dont: Tilt the phone up or down
Lift it overhead

steps.title: Walk the set path
steps.body: Follow the on-screen path. Loop each room about 1 m from the walls, then cross the doorway into the next room.
steps.diagram_alt: Virtual Visit walking path: loop each room, cross doorways twice
do: Cross every doorway twice
Keep doors open
dont: Skip corners
Walk in front of mirrors

steps.title: Walk slowly
steps.body: Follow the on-screen pace: about 0.5 m per second, or 1 m every 2 seconds.
steps.diagram_alt: Virtual Visit walking speed, about 0.5 m/s
do: Keep a steady pace
dont: Stop and start
Turn quickly

steps.title: Reset the home
steps.body: Put back anything you moved. Leave lights and blinds as you found them.
do: Lock up as agreed
dont: Leave gear marks or moved items

steps.title: Check your lists
steps.body: Every shot and clip ID must be done or marked "not possible" with a reason.
do: Review the hero exterior and key clips on site
dont: Leave without checking

steps.title: Name your files
steps.body: Clips: JobID_ClipID_T1.mov. Stills: keep the camera's file names. The app groups each set from its exposure data.
do: Add _V before the take for vertical clips
Name by hand only as stem_-2, stem_0, stem_+2
dont: Rename with tools that strip metadata

steps.title: Upload clips
steps.body: Upload original camera files in the app within 6 hours of wrap. Mark the best take.
do: One best take, one alternate at most
dont: Transcode, compress or send proxies

steps.title: Upload RAW stills
steps.body: Upload every bracket frame as a camera RAW, straight out of camera, within 6 hours of wrap. Bricks edits, reviews and exports every still.
do: RAW brackets plus the window frame and any flash frame
CR2, CR3, NEF, ARW, RAF, ORF, RW2, DNG, PEF or SRW, EXIF intact
JPEG only if a RAW is over 50 MB
Keep your RAWs until the job is approved
dont: Edit, merge or apply a preset
Export JPEGs when the RAW fits
Make MLS sizes or add watermarks

add_horizontal: INT-10 (second time of light, if the schedule allows)

limits.stills_upload: Unedited camera RAW bracket frames plus the window frame, EXIF intact. JPEG only for a RAW over 50 MB. Keep RAWs until approval.

plus: flash frame where light is mixed

devices.stills: Dedicated camera, 24 MP or more, RAW + JPEG. No phones. Capture only: Bricks edits.
devices.clips: Dedicated camera with gimbal, slider or tripod. No phones.

approved: iPhone 13 Pro or newer Pro models

naming.still_note: Keep camera file names; the app groups sets from EXIF exposure data.
